source.title: Interpretability Transfer from Language to Vision via Sparse Autoencoders
source.authors: Alexey Kravets; Da Li; Chuan Li; Da Chen; Vinay Namboodiri

record.file_problem: None; the full paper and supplementary material are present.
record.tranche_reason: It measures SAE-based semantic recovery and localization in multimodal models and tests interventions using SAE directions, rather than reproducing the toy-model method. Its results bear on V4, indirect evidence for SAE-recoverable features in real models.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results on SAE matching, feature reconstruction and sparsity, spatial localization, and concept interventions. The SAE-constrained results are deliberately induced by the training objective; they are recorded as results but are not evidence that the same alignment arises naturally. Benchmark performance comparisons unrelated to the claim are omitted. The paper describes some matching-rate and reconstruction results only in figures, without numerical values.
record.test_reason: VISTA uses pre-trained text SAEs (Gemma Scope, LLaMA Scope) as a tool. It trains a visual projector so visual tokens become reconstructible by those SAEs, then reports its own method's matching, localization and steering against baselines. It does not test whether LLMs naturally contain SAE-recoverable sparse features (V4) or any other version. The VISTA-constrained results are induced by the training objective. The unconstrained 'delayed alignment' results ask whether visual tokens fit a text SAE, which is a different construct from V4.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that an SAE reconstruction loss on the projector transfers text-SAE interpretability to visual tokens. It gives roughly threefold higher matching rates and steering gains of 35% (removal) and 47% (replacement) over vision-SAE baselines. Natural delayed alignment holds for Gemma but not LLaMA, and localized interpretability depends on the encoder, with DINOv2 best.
record.recipe_differences: The paper trains a multimodal visual projector with an SAE reconstruction constraint and evaluates SAE-based matching, localization, and interventions; it does not use toy networks or test the original superposition method.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary with LLM architecture and visual encoder. The paper reports natural later-layer alignment for Gemma but not unconstrained LLaMA; DINOv2 localization is high across tested backbones, while CLIP localization varies and remains lower. OOD matching is lower than in-distribution matching.

fits_no_version.finding: Without SAE constraints, visual tokens fit text SAEs only in late layers for Gemma 2B/9B (high error and density early, later convergence, rising match rate). For LLaMA-3.1-8B they never converge and the match rate stays low.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Natural late-layer alignment of visual tokens with a text-SAE feature space ('delayed alignment') is architecture-dependent.

fits_no_version.finding: Adding or subtracting text-SAE decoder directions on localized visual tokens steers object removal and replacement. Mean score is up to 1.56 with VISTA+DINOv2, versus 0.00-0.49 for no-SAE projectors, and stays low with CLIP.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Text-SAE directions can causally steer visual tokens once a projector is trained into the SAE manifold (an engineered, not natural, alignment).

record.code_released: not stated; the text says code is available on GitHub but gives no URL.
record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 306, 2026.
record.problems: Matching-rate and reconstruction/sparsity plots generally lack tabulated numerical values. The paper reports no uncertainty estimates. Some OOD table entries do not identify the model configuration. The SAE-constrained alignment and steering are deliberately induced by training, so they do not alone establish naturally occurring alignment.
record.rows_left_out: The remaining SAE steering configurations from Table 7 are included for all encoders and backbones; no results were omitted from that table. Other benchmark-performance results were left out because they do not directly measure the claim.

untested.parts: No toy models, sparsity transition or geometry.
No analysis of alternative causes of polysemanticity.
Uses existing text SAEs as given. It does not measure whether LLM activations naturally spread features or whether SAEs recover sparse features in them.
SAE completeness, stability or canonicity are not evaluated.
No comparison of 1-D and multi-dimensional features.

record.verdict_notes: Re-classified from tests/T2 to uses_without_test/T4, so the reader's V4 labels are dropped. The paper's evidence is its own engineered method's performance. Its natural-alignment baselines measure whether visual tokens fit a text SAE, not whether LLMs contain SAE-recoverable features. Superposition is only cited (Elhage et al. 2022) as motivation for using SAEs. No uncertainty estimates are reported. Many results are figure-only.

versions.untested_parts: Toy networks, feature sparsity and importance, superposition geometry, and transitions.
Whether features compete for capacity or important features receive dedicated dimensions; performance regressions under SAE constraints do not test this account.
Alternative causes of polysemantic neurons and whether polysemanticity is evidence of superposition.
The paper studies multimodal visual-token features, not whether language-model features generally spread across many neurons; its SAE-constrained results are induced by training.
Whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units is not directly evaluated.
No comparison of one-dimensional directions with multidimensional features.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Unconstrained Gemma-2-2B-it visual tokens, especially later layers
reader_labels.reason: The paper reports that natural SAE concept matching improves in later layers and Gemma visual tokens align with text features in deeper layers (r10, r37).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: Natural matching remains low and stagnant, and reconstruction error and density stay high rather than converging (r12, r38).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Spatial localization across encoders and LLM backbones under VISTA
reader_labels.reason: SAE concept localization varies substantially by encoder: DINOv2 scores highly, while CLIP is much lower; I-JEPA lies between them (r1-r9).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: Matching remains substantial but falls from 0.63 in-distribution to 0.58 OOD (r15, r16).
